HARD RULE: nothing here may state a fact about the business. No menu
items, no prices, no hours, no address. Those come from their own site or
But 'no facts' must not become 'empty page'. For a shop with no website
the demo IS the entire pitch, and a page of empty boxes says 'you have
nothing' when it needs to say 'look what this could be'. So a thin harvest
gets MORE craft, not less: every section fully designed, populated with
visibly-labelled sample rows, plus the capability strip below.

capability_showcase.intro: When a section has no real data, do NOT reduce it to a sentence in a box. Build the section out fully, in the chosen art direction, using sample rows that are obviously labelled as samples. The owner must see the finished shape and the quality of the craft.
techniques: A sticky header that condenses as the page scrolls (CSS position: sticky, no JavaScript).
Menu sections as native <details>/<summary> accordions — expandable, keyboard accessible, zero script.
A horizontal photo strip using scroll-snap, if any photographs exist.
Real hover and focus states on every link and button, with a visible focus ring.
tel: and mailto: links so a phone taps straight through to a call.
prefers-color-scheme: a considered dark variant, not an inverted one.
Inline SVG for any mark, divider or icon — never an image file, never an emoji.
capability_showcase.sample_row_rule: Sample rows carry generic labels ('Your signature dish', 'Second course') and an em dash where a price would sit. Never a number that could be mistaken for their pricing.

no_image_treatment: With no photographs, the type and colour must carry the whole page — a large wordmark over a considered colour field, an inline SVG texture at low opacity, and generous scale. This is a chance to show craft, not a reason to make the page thin.
